title: View of the Hebrews; exhibiting the destruction of Jerusalem (1st ed.)
author: Ethan Smith
evidence: Printed Poultney, Vt.: Smith & Shute, 1823. Advertised and reviewed 1823-1824 in Vermont and eastern New York (Poultney Gazette 10 Dec 1823; Saratoga Sentinel 23 and 30 Dec 1823; Ballston Spa Gazette 20 Apr 1824), per the sourced B. H. Roberts Foundation timeline. No Palmyra, Ontario or Wayne County ad found; the Wayne Sentinel OCR has no hit for the title (OCR misses are not negatives). Indirect only: Josiah Priest's Wonders of Nature and Providence (Albany 1825), which reprints VOTH ch. 3, is Manchester Library no. 208 but Paul documents its circulation only 'by late 1836'.

title: View of the Hebrews; or the Tribes of Israel in America (2nd ed.)
author: Ethan Smith
evidence: Printed Poultney, Vt.: Smith & Shute, 1825. 'JUST Received' by Merrell & Hastings, 40 Genesee Street, Utica, N.Y.: Western Recorder, 7 Feb 1826, p. 23 ('New Books'), giving the 2nd-edition title. Utica is central New York, about 140 miles east of Palmyra. No Palmyra/Canandaigua ad or library holding found.

title: The Late War, between the United States and Great Britain
author: Gilbert J. Hunt
evidence: Printed New York: David Longworth, 1816; reissued 1817 and 1819 as 'The Historical Reader' for schools. A title 'Historical Reader' is advertised in Palmyra book lists 27 Jul 1827-28 May 1830 (Wayne Sentinel OCR, 22 pages) with no author named, and J. L. Blake's different 'Historical Reader' (Concord, N.H., 1824-1825 onward) was also in print. Checked on the page scans (26 Oct 1827 p4, Palmyra Bookstore; 20 Mar 1829 p4 and 11 Dec 1829 p3, E. B. Grandin): every entry is a bare 'Historical Reader' among school books, with no author, price or subtitle, so it cannot be assigned to Hunt. Not in T. C. Strong's 1818 Palmyra list (Palmyra Register, 15 Sep 1818 p3, read on the scan), though Hunt's 1817 Historical Reader was then in print, nor in the Strong & Bradish list of 1819; no Hunt title in the Palmyra Register (1817-1821) or Palmyra Herald (1822-1823) OCR. A satirical piece in the Register (9 Aug 1820 p3) mocks a 'History of the late war' published at Hartford in 1815 and sold by pedlars: a different book (Hunt's is New York 1816). Unresolved; would be a 3 if shown to be Hunt's.

title: The First Book of Napoleon, the Tyrant of the Earth
author: 'Eliakim the Scribe' (attrib. Michael Linning)
evidence: Imprint London: Longman, Hurst, Rees & Orme; J. J. Stockdale, 1809 (Edinburgh and Dublin sellers on the title page). No American printing found in Internet Archive or the web sources searched; no US ad found. Not established that it circulated in the US before 1829.

title: Manuscript Story ('Manuscript Found')
author: Solomon Spalding
evidence: Unpublished manuscript; Spalding died 1816; first printed 1885 (Lamoni: RLDS). Holograph at Oberlin College Archives RG 30/028. Claims that it reached Palmyra rest on recollections collected from 1833 (E. D. Howe, Mormonism Unvailed, 1834), not on any contemporary document. No documentary evidence that it circulated before 1829.
